reason: Conversation 1 gives a generic stop-and-unplug notice but nothing else: no questions about unplugged tripping or tingles, no out-of-scope statement, no diagnosis, and it steers toward an engineer check rather than the sensible outcome of retiring a cheap kettle. Conversation 2 correctly identifies RCD earth leakage from the kettle, elicits the key facts (water in base, tingle, crackle), then delivers the critical safety stop clearly: unplug with dry hands, bin the kettle, don't dry and reuse, replace it, electrician only if trips persist. Its first turn is weaker on safety (it suggests testing the kettle on another circuit and only cautions against using it rather than ordering an immediate stop) and it never notes kettles are outside the service, which keeps the margin from being decisive.
